items.titleJa: TypeScriptのasを減らす：satisfiesとの使い分けを実例で整理する
items.summaryJa: TypeScript では as の代わりに satisfies を使う場面が多く、型推論を保ちつつ型の適合性を検証できる点が特徴です。本文は、as は型を「検証する」よりも「この型として扱ってよいと伝える」型アサーションであり、実行時値を変えない点、誤用時の不整合を招く可能性がある点を説明します。一方 satisfies は値が指定の型を満たすかを検証し、具体的な型情報を維持しやすい利点を挙げ、設定オブジェクトや定数テーブル、キー漏れ検出など実務での活用例を多数紹介します。さらに型注釈や as const との使い分け、外部データの検証時には satisfies だけでは不十分な場合がある点を補足します。実務では、型推論に任せられるときはそれを優先し、設定やマッピングには satisfies、特定の型として扱う必要がある場合は型注釈、リテラルを保持したい場合は as const、という順序・使い分けが推奨されています。

items.titleJa: Claude CodeのEffortについておさらい

items.title: FastAPI frontends and static files served from the CDN
items.summary: FastAPI frontends and static files, served with app.frontend() or StaticFiles , are now promoted to the Vercel CDN at build time. Requests for those paths are served directly from the CDN, without invoking your Vercel Function. FastAPI evaluates routes in declaration order. A route declared before a StaticFiles mount takes priority over any CDN file at that path. This precedence is preserved. Promoted source directories remain in the function bundle so the app can read from them at runtime. To exclude them and serve only from the CDN, set tool.vercel.fastapi.static.exclude = true in pyproject.toml . Frontends guarded by dependencies are kept on the function as the CDN cannot run dependency checks. Similarly, static files which sit behind middleware are also kept on the function. To override this and always promote to CDN, set tool.vercel.fastapi.static.cdn = true . To opt out of the CDN entirely, set it to false instead. For more information see the Vercel FastAPI documentation . Read more
items.titleJa: FastAPI frontends and static files served from the CDN

items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​757 — September 9, 2026 | Read on the web New Things You Should Know About HTML in 2026 — HTML moves a bit slower than CSS and JavaScript, but there's plenty of new features to keep up with. Chris runs through several, including the geolocation element, HTML-in-Canvas, camera and mic management via usermedia , and the model element. A great way to catch up. Chris Coyier The Best Dark Mode Toggle is Probably… None — We recently shared some thoughts from Lea on controls for switching between light/dark modes. After weeks of debate, including a rebuttal from Bramus , she returns to ask whether most sites need an always-visible toggle at all . Lea Verou Free Course: Build Ambitious Modern Interfaces Faster with OpenAI Codex — Join Katia Gil Guzman for this free Codex course and learn how agentic coding has changed frontend development. You'll cover setup, prompting, feedback, skills, automations, deployment and more. Master.dev sponsor Antiquated HTML Snippets and Artefacts — A tour of various snippets of code that commonly appear in HTML, but which are largely byproducts of a bygone era and are no longer needed. Conditional comments, X-UA-Compatible , and cleartype directives all make an appearance. Declan Chidlow 🗳️ W3C Opens Its 2026 Community Survey — The W3C has launched its 2026 community-wide survey to gather input from developers and stakeholders on the future direction of its operations and web standards work. W3C ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🎉 The team behind Tailwind CSS is joining Shopify but "nothing changes with Tailwind CSS or any of our other open-source projects." 📑 Interop 2027 proposals are open until September 23 — you can nominate the cross-browser gaps that most need fixing. 🗓️ As promised, Chrome has now moved to a two-week release cycle , with Firefox, Edge and Brave following suit. 🖼️ JPEG XL support will be enabled by default in Firefox 158 . 🕵️ Years ago, a developer noticed Chrome exempted Google's own sites from the setting that wipes site data on exit (Google fixed it). Now, he claims it's happening again as of Chrome 152 . 🏛️ InfoQ reflects on jQuery 1.0 turning 20 years old and why it remains heavily used across the Web. 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials Creating a Custom Scrollbar Component in 2026 — How to approach building high-performance custom scrollbars, replacing heavy JavaScript arithmetic with modern CSS features and handling sizing and visibility entirely within the stylesheet. A clean, modern approach to a classic UI challenge. Alexander Inkin The Browser's Main Thread is Expensive — A thorough look, complete with demos, at spending your main thread time well, including splitting, batching, prioritizing, and deferring tasks, then how to get work off it entirely. Sunhyoup Lee The Loading State Isn't the Frontend's Fault — It's the query behind it. TimescaleDB extends Postgres so it returns fast as data grows. Get $1000 credit to start . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor Wiring Up Components with Typed attr() and Container Style Queries — Shows how to feed HTML attributes into CSS properties (like grid column counts or spacing units), then let style queries pass that state down to child components with no JavaScript state or utility classes required. Brecht De Ruyte CSS: The Weapon Inside Your Inbox — How CSS can be weaponized against popular webmail providers to do things it shouldn't be able to, like defacing the UI, bypassing image proxies, and building a keylogger. Gareth Heyes Testing Cookie Behavior Across Hundreds of Web Surfaces with an In-House Auditor — An interesting ‘big corp’ case study looking at tooling built to audit cookie behavior at scale across various web properties. Yasmin McDowell and Lawrence Good (Dropbox) .name Termination — Discusses the impending sunset of .name 's third-level domains and the implications for those using it for their online identity. Neil Fraser Building an Infinite Liquid Glass Grid with Three.js, WebGPU, and TSL Filip Kantedal (Codrops) 🦖 How the Chrome Dino Game Works: A Tour of Chromium's Source Alex Oliinyk Animating CSS Grid Layouts with CSS Anchor Positioning Bramus van Damme 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources Drawably: Hand-Drawn UI Controls — A collection of neat hand-drawn UI controls. The animated pen sketches even get drawn via seeded randomness. Zero dependencies, ~7 KB of JS gzipped and a 3 KB stylesheet. Repo here . Daniel White vgpu: Render WebGPU Shaders in the Browser or Node.js — Provides a way to use the same shader in the browser or render headlessly with Node (to a high-resolution PNG or MP4 video). WGSL modules import and export like TypeScript does. Vercel Sentry Says It Crashed. Datadog Says It's Slow. Expo Tells You Why — Expo Observe knows your release pipeline, so it ties a startup regression to the exact build or update that caused it. Expo sponsor WCAG Radar: Run Accessibility Checks on Pages You Have Open — A bookmarklet and browser extension that runs WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 AA checks against the page you’re on and marks up the results in place, all running locally. Note: 28 of the checks are free, but you get 18 additional checks with a paid upgrade. Proper Access B.V. Roux: A Boilerplate of Pre-Defined Native CSS Styling — This HTML/CSS starter provides a foundation of CSS files, variables, base styles, and HTML components. You can see it in action on the docs page . thoughtbot The Fixi Project: A Collection of Small Web Libraries by the Creators of htmx — All five libraries – each one a standalone script – are designed to be lightweight versions of their more popular offerings like htmx, Hyperscript, Idiomorph, etc. Source code . Big Sky Software 📰 Classifieds 📸 Scan barcodes, QR codes and others directly in the browser using STRICH , a lean JS SDK. Free 14-day trial, try the demo app today! 🔎 A Minimal Browser for macOS Confectionery: A Browser for Taking Cleaner Screenshots — A Mac-only browser with a stripped-back UI ideal for taking tidy screenshots with minimal browser clutter. Only a 2.9MB download too. Vadim Demedes

Its new architecture processes input and generates output with separate components, reducing the active computation needed for each stage. Use deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try DeepSeek V4.1 Flash in the model playground . It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.
